name: Multi-Issue Packaging (Logrolling)
scenario: Negotiating enterprise software licensing where the buyer demands a price point below the seller's strict software gross margin threshold.
script: "We cannot drop our annual subscription licensing fee to $180,000 in isolation. However, if your team is willing to execute a three-year commitment, pay the entirety upfront within fifteen days, and agree to participate in two industry case studies, we can deliver the $180,000 annual pricing."
defense: Enforce the package: $180,000 is contingent on prepayment and case studies; unbundled, the fee returns to $230,000.
originFull: Pareto-Optimal Trade-off Theory in Multi-Attribute Decision Making shows that value is created when negotiators trade issues that are low-cost to one party but high-value to the other.
defenseFull: When an aggressive buyer attempts to accept the concession while rejecting the package, enforce structural linkage: "The $180,000 pricing is fundamentally contingent on the cash acceleration and marketing rights. If we unbundle those provisions, the standalone annual software fee reverts to our baseline of $230,000."
